intro.data: Now there are THREE content types in a chain (User → Email → Host), so there are TWO naturality squares to satisfy at once. At each type you again get the trustworthy 'first item' converter and the cheating 'first-or-a-made-up-default' one. A single slip anywhere breaks a square. Pick the natural converter at all three.
intro.alchemy: Now there are THREE reagents in a chain, so there are TWO naturality squares to satisfy at once. At each reagent you again get the trustworthy 'Take First' method and the cheating 'First or Conjure' one. A single slip anywhere breaks a square. Pick the natural method at all three.
intro.spellcraft: Now there are THREE essences in a chain, so there are TWO naturality squares to satisfy at once. At each essence you again get the trustworthy 'Take Top' working and the cheating 'Top or Conjure' one. A single slip anywhere breaks a square. Pick the natural working at all three.
intro.abstract: C has three objects A→B→C, giving two naturality squares (for f and g). Choose components α_A, α_B, α_C so both α_B∘F(f)=G(f)∘α_A and α_C∘F(g)=G(g)∘α_B hold.

afterSuccess.data: You picked the trustworthy 'first item' converter at all three types, and BOTH naturality squares commuted at once. A natural transformation has to be natural everywhere — one cheating component anywhere would have broken a square. safeHead is natural across the whole chain.
afterSuccess.alchemy: You picked 'Take First' at all three reagents, and BOTH squares commuted at once. A natural transformation has to be natural everywhere — one cheating method would have broken a square.
afterSuccess.spellcraft: You chose 'Take Top' at all three essences, and BOTH squares commuted at once. A natural transformation has to be natural everywhere — one cheating working would have broken a square.
afterSuccess.abstract: Both squares commute with α = safeHead at every object: α_B∘F(f)=G(f)∘α_A and α_C∘F(g)=G(g)∘α_B. Naturality is a condition at every morphism, not just one.

reveal.summary: Naturality must hold at EVERY morphism of C: for each f, α_target ∘ F(f) = G(f) ∘ α_source. A family is a natural transformation only when all of its squares commute together.
reveal.programmerAnalogy: A polymorphic function that's natural for every function in the chain, not just one.
